page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8y.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the 64-bit ARM architecture, powered by Alibaba's custom 2.75 GHz YiTian710 processor. The instance allocates 32 dedicated physical cores across 32 vCPUs with a single thread per core, accompanied by 64 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 64 KB L1 data cache per core. Memory capacity is 64.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core. The platform operates on a KVM hypervisor and provides a baseline network throughput of 16 Gbps. No local storage is bundled with the instance, requiring reliance on external network-attached volumes, and no GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong throughput in multi-threaded data processing and memory tasks. The 32 physical cores achieve top-quartile performance in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 267.02 GB/s, alongside strong ratings in PassMark memory testing (2948.80) and database operations (26041.42). General processing metrics place the instance in the middle 50% tier, with a multi-core stress-ng score of 57749.33 and a PassMark CPU score of 22894.56. In-memory data throughput registers 50.47 million Redis SET operations per second, while static web serving achieves 35.0 GB/s. For language model inferencing, the instance delivers 1198.39 prompt tokens per second on a small 135M model and 41.79 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

Hardware tradeoffs center around the compute-heavy architectural profile. Dedicated 1:1 physical core mapping prevents hyperthreading contention and ensures deterministic execution performance under sustained multithreaded loads. However, the 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio makes it inefficient for memory-intensive caching or in-memory analytics. In addition, the ARM64 platform lacks x86 AVX instruction extensions, although hardware-level AES cryptographic acceleration is present. The server offers high resource density for workloads scaled horizontally, matching CPU-bound parallel processing, container clusters, microservices tiers, CI/CD compilation, and web serving infrastructures.
